'''Matthew Peter Scott''' is an American biologist who was the tenth president of the Carnegie Institution for Science.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/matthew-scott | title=Matthew P. Scott's Profile &#124; Stanford Profiles }}</ref> While at [[Stanford University]], Scott studied how embryonic and later development is governed by proteins that control [[gene]] activity and [[cell signaling]] processes.<ref name=ScottlabStanford>{{cite web
| url=http://scottlab.stanford.edu/
| title=Scott lab homepage at Stanford University
| access-date=2009-04-10
| archive-date=2008-12-04
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081204010423/http://scottlab.stanford.edu/
| url-status=dead
}}</ref><ref name=ScottHHMI>{{cite web
| url=http://www.hhmi.org/research/investigators/scottm_bio.html
| title=HHMI Scientist Bio: Matthew P. Scott, Ph.D.
| access-date=2009-04-10
}}</ref> He co-discovered [[homeobox]] genes in ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' working with Amy J. Weiner at [[Indiana University]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Scott| first1 = M. P. |author-link1 = Matthew P. Scott and A. ==Education==
Scott completed a B.S. in 1975 and Ph.D. in biology in 1980, both at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matthew P. Scott's Profile {{!}} Stanford Profiles |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/matthew-scott |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=profiles.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Scott served on the faculty of the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]] starting in 1983. He moved to [[Stanford University]] in 1990 to join the faculty of the Department of Developmental Biology and the Department of Genetics. From 2002-2007 he served as Chair of Bio-X, Stanford's interdisciplinary biosciences program.<ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.cgm.northwestern.edu/cgm/Academics/Richard-A.-Scott-MD-Lecture-Series/Biography-Matthew-Scott
| title=Biography: Matthew Scott
| publisher=Center for Genetic Medicine, [[Northwestern University]]
| access-date=2009-04-10
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620145903/https://www.cgm.northwestern.edu/cgm/Academics/Richard-A.-Scott-MD-Lecture-Series/Biography-Matthew-Scott
| archive-date=2010-06-20
| url-status=dead
}}</ref>
